sections.h2: What the Greenup County Clerk does in a sale
sections.html:
The Clerk puts a sale on the public record by recording the deed and any new mortgage. Deeds go to the clerk of the county where the land sits, so a house in Greenup, Flatwoods, Raceland, Russell, South Shore, Worthington or Wurtland is recorded here. Documents can arrive through an e-recording vendor or be carried to a counter. Ask the title company or closing attorney who handles the recording and the transfer tax, and keep the recorded copy for your files.

The office also takes unpaid tax bills the sheriff passes along after April 15 and runs the sale of those bills. Our Greenup County property tax guide covers the sheriff and PVA side.

Three offices serve the county, each open Monday to Friday, 9:00 a.m. until 4:30 p.m. The South Shore branch closes for lunch between noon and 1:00 p.m. Mail for the main office goes to PO Box 686, Greenup, KY 41144.

  • Main office, Greenup County Courthouse, Room 208: (606) 473-7394, fax (606) 473-5354.
  • Flatwoods branch, 2513 Reed Street, Suite 3: (606) 836-1944, fax (606) 836-1444.
  • South Shore branch, 69 Narco Drive: (606) 932-6564, fax (606) 932-3691.

Court problems go to the Circuit Clerk at (606) 473-9869, and vehicle questions go to drive.ky.gov. Before you drive anywhere with a deed, ask whether a branch can record it or whether it has to go to the main office. The Clerk is closed on weekends and posts holiday hours on its website.

A deed costs $50 for its first five pages and $3 for each page after that, with transfer tax added on top. The Clerk's Records page lists a minimum for each type of document.

Selected Greenup County Clerk recording fees
DocumentMinimum fee
Deed, easement, power of attorney or plat$50

A state tax lien is only $5, while a federal lien filing is $46. A document with no specific statutory fee is charged $46. Since these are minimums, confirm the fee for your exact document before you mail a check.

sections.h2: Transfer tax on a Greenup County sale
sections.html:
The tax is $1.00 for each $1,000.00 paid for the property, collected when the deed is recorded. The amount follows the price stated for the property, so the closing statement and the deed should match. Your contract decides who pays it, and the closing agent can confirm. It appears as a separate line from the recording fee, so add the two for a rough total.

A deed that transfers a house for no money, such as a gift inside a family, can raise questions about which tax and wording apply. Ask the Clerk's office before you sign.

The Clerk lists five e-recording vendors: Indecomm, Hopdox, CSC, Simplifile and ePN. A closing agent can submit documents through any of them without a trip to the courthouse. Records can be searched online through eCCLIX, the online version of the County Clerk Indexing system, which almost two-thirds of Kentucky's clerk offices use. Attorneys, title searchers, surveyors and realtors rely on it.

  • Private citizens searching for personal reasons can use Greenup County records at no charge, up to five searches a day.
  • Commercial users such as title searchers and surveyors pay a subscription and can add other counties.
  • eCCLIX lets users view or print documents filed by more than 85 Kentucky clerk offices.

sections.h2: Liens and probate papers the Clerk records
sections.html:
The recording schedule covers more than deeds. Several items on it come up when a house is inherited or has a dispute attached.

  • Affidavit of descent, $50, and will, $47: papers an heir often records to show how a house passed.
  • Power of attorney, $50, and its revocation, $46.
  • Inheritance tax lien and its release, $5 each.
  • State tax lien, $5, against $46 for a federal tax lien and $46 for its release.
  • Mechanic lien, $46, and a bond to release a mechanic lien, $60.
  • Judgment lien and lis pendens notice, $46 each.
  • Child support lien, $5 in state and $46 out of state.
  • Deed of restrictions, condominium declaration and plat, $50 each; easement release, $46.

A recorded lien shows up in a buyer's title search, so find out which ones are on file before you sell. Each release is its own filing with its own fee, recorded in the same office. Ask the Clerk for current copies of any lien you find.

sections.h2: Steps from signed deed to recorded deed
sections.html:
Most sellers never visit the Clerk. The usual path runs like this. The closing agent collects the signed deed and the money for the transfer tax and recording fee. The deed goes to the Clerk by an e-recording vendor or by hand. The Clerk takes the fees, records the deed and indexes it, and the recorded copy comes back to the buyer.

If you are paying off a mortgage, the lender's release is a separate filing with its own fee, and it should reach the same office. Ask the closing agent to confirm both the deed and the release were recorded. A cash buyer who closes quickly follows the same steps, minus any lender paperwork.

DOCALERT is a free service the Clerk's office offers through Software Management, LLC. Signing up takes a name and an email address. After that, any mortgage or deed filed in Greenup County under your personal or business name triggers a message to you.

It suits anyone who owns a house they do not live in: a landlord, an heir holding a parent's home, or the owner of a vacant property. If a deed or mortgage you never signed gets recorded, the message gives you a reason to call the Clerk and an attorney right away.

sections.h2: Delinquent property tax at the Clerk
sections.html:
Every unpaid real property bill reaches the Clerk from the sheriff on April 15, and a lien is recorded against each parcel. Bills still open later are sold. The Clerk's delinquent taxes page links purchaser information, an application and the state's delinquent tax listing.

The state process puts the sale 90 to 135 days after the transfer. The county attorney sends notices, and bills are advertised 30 to 45 days ahead. Interest runs at 1 percent per month, with commissions and a lien recording and release fee on top. Payments before the sale go through the Clerk. After it, the lien belongs to a third-party purchaser and you pay that buyer.

If your bill is already at the Clerk, get the payoff in writing and have it paid from proceeds, so the lien release is recorded alongside the deed.

faqs.q: What does the Greenup County Clerk charge for a deed?
faqs.a: $50 covers the first five pages, and each added page is $3. Transfer tax of $1.00 per $1,000 paid goes on top. Call the office for the total on your document.

faqs.q: When is the Greenup County Clerk open?
faqs.a: Weekdays from 9:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. at the courthouse, Flatwoods and South Shore offices. South Shore closes for lunch from noon to 1:00 p.m.

faqs.q: What phone numbers reach the Greenup County Clerk?
Do Greenup County residents pay to search land records?
faqs.a: No, personal searches through eCCLIX are free up to five a day. Businesses that research records pay a subscription.
